1: # Contracts (MVP)
2: 
3: The interfaces between the three [work packages](work-packages.md). If something here doesn't fit, raise it with the team before coding around it.
4: 
5: ## Stack
6: 
7: | Part | Choice |
8: | --- | --- |
9: | Frontend (iPhone) | SwiftUI, iOS 17+, `URLSessionWebSocketTask`, `AVAudioEngine`, [a2ui-swift](https://github.com/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift) `from: "0.3.0"` (product `A2UISwiftUI`) |
10: | Backend | Python 3.11, uv, FastAPI and uvicorn, httpx, `google-genai`, `gradium`, python-dotenv, pytest |
11: | Hosting | Server on a dev Mac; a Cloudflare quick tunnel gives the HTTPS and WSS URL that the app and the Shortcut use. Start it once and leave it running: the URL changes on every restart |
12: | Time zone | `Europe/Zurich` everywhere; times on the wire are ISO 8601 with offset |
13: 
14: ```text
15: frontend/               # WP1: Xcode project, SwiftUI
16: backend/                # run from here: uv run uvicorn app:app --reload --port 8000
17:   pyproject.toml        # WP2 owns it; lists every package's deps
18:   .env.example
19:   app.py  voice.py  vision.py      # WP2
20:   a2ui.py                          # WP3: cards → A2UI messages
21:   agent.py  context.py  tools/sbb.py   # WP3
22:   fixtures/             # demo_reply.json, cards.json, screen.json, screen.png (WP2); context.json, *_a2ui.json (WP3)
23:   tests/
24: ```
25: 
26: ## One turn
27: 
28: The screenshot arrives before the question, so vision runs while the user is still talking.
29: 
30: ```mermaid
31: sequenceDiagram
32:   participant SC as Shortcut
33:   participant App as App (WP1)
34:   participant S as Server (WP2)
35:   participant V as Vision (WP2)
36:   participant G as Gradium
37:   participant A as Agent (WP3)
38:   SC->>S: POST /screenshot
39:   S->>V: read_screen(image), in the background
40:   V-->>S: ScreenContext
41:   S->>App: screen_ok {summary}
42:   App->>S: audio × n, then audio_end
43:   S->>G: stream mic audio, flush
44:   G-->>S: transcript segments
45:   S->>App: state thinking, transcript
46:   S->>A: turn(text, screen, on_status)
47:   A-->>S: on_status("Checking trains…")
48:   S->>App: state searching + label
49:   A-->>S: Reply {say, cards}
50:   S->>App: reply, a2ui, state speaking
51:   S->>G: TTS say
52:   G-->>S: audio chunks
53:   S->>App: audio × n, audio_end, state idle
54: ```
55: 
56: ## WebSocket `/ws`
57: 
58: JSON text frames only, one object per frame, discriminated by `type`. Audio is base64 inside JSON. The app sends `hello` first; the server closes the socket on a wrong token.
59: 
60: **App → server**
61: 
62: | `type` | Fields | When |
63: | --- | --- | --- |
64: | `hello` | `token` | First frame after connecting |
65: | `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM, see [Audio](#audio) | Every 80 ms while the orb is held |
66: | `audio_end` | — | Orb released; the server finalizes STT and runs the turn |
67: | `text` | `text` | Typed question (debug field); runs a turn without STT |
68: | `screen` | `mime`, `data`: base64 | Optional: an image picked in the app, for rehearsals. Same effect as `POST /screenshot` |
69: 
70: **Server → app**
71: 
72: | `type` | Fields | When |
73: | --- | --- | --- |
74: | `ready` | — | After a valid `hello` |
75: | `state` | `state`: `idle` \| `listening` \| `thinking` \| `searching` \| `speaking`; `label`?: string | On every change; `label` is the tool status, e.g. "Checking trains…" |
76: | `transcript` | `text` | Final transcript of the user's turn |
77: | `reply` | `say`, `cards`: see [Cards](#cards) | Before any of the turn's audio |
78: | `a2ui` | `messages`: list of A2UI v0.9 messages, see [A2UI](#a2ui) | Right after `reply`, when it has cards |
79: | `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM | TTS chunks for the last `reply` |
80: | `audio_end` | — | TTS for the last `reply` is complete |
81: | `screen_ok` | `summary`?: string | Vision has read a new screenshot; `summary` is missing if vision failed |
82: | `error` | `message` | Turn failed; the server then sends `state: idle` |
83: 
84: The orb shows `speaking` while the app still has audio queued, even after the server has sent `state: idle`.
85: 
86: ## HTTP
87: 
88: | Route | Contract |
89: | --- | --- |
90: | `POST /screenshot` | From the iPhone Shortcut. `Authorization: Bearer <APP_TOKEN>`, body is the raw image (`image/jpeg` or `image/png`, max 8 MB). Returns `204` and starts vision |
91: | `GET /health` | `{"ok": true, "workspace": "rest" \| "fixture"}` |
92: 
93: **Screenshot rule:** the server keeps only the latest screenshot and its `ScreenContext`. A turn gets the context if the screenshot is less than 120 s old and no earlier turn has used it; if vision is still running, the turn waits for it.
94: 
95: ## Audio
96: 
97: Both directions use Gradium's native format, so the server forwards the base64 strings without decoding them.
98: 
99: | Direction | Format | Gradium side |
100: | --- | --- | --- |
101: | Mic, app → server | PCM signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 24 kHz; 80 ms chunks = 1920 samples = 3840 bytes | STT setup `input_format: "pcm"` |
102: | TTS, server → app | Same format, chunks as Gradium sends them | TTS setup `output_format: "pcm_24000"` (the default `pcm` is 48 kHz) |
103: 
104: **iPhone side:** audio session `.playAndRecord` with `.defaultToSpeaker`, or iOS plays through the quiet earpiece while the mic is on. Turn on echo cancellation with `inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)` before reading the input format. Convert the input with `AVAudioConverter` to Int16 at 24 kHz mono. Play through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` on the same engine, converting each chunk to a Float32 24 kHz buffer.
105: 
106: **Gradium facts the server relies on** ([docs](https://docs.gradium.ai/api-reference/introduction)): auth header `x-api-key`; STT at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/asr`, TTS at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/tts`; the Python SDK is `pip install gradium`. STT needs `json_config.language` (`en` for the demo, `any` to auto-detect). STT sends `text` segments, not partial and final flags. On push-to-talk release the server sends `flush`, waits for `flushed`, and joins the segments into the transcript. TTS has no cancel message: closing the socket stops it. The free plan allows 2 TTS and 3 STT sessions at once, which is tight with 3 devs testing; the $13 XS plan raises that to 5 and 20.
107: 
108: ## Cards
109: 
110: `reply.cards` holds 0 to 3 cards. The model fills them from tool results and context, and the server passes them through after validation. Optional fields may be missing. The app renders the `a2ui` messages built from these cards; native SwiftUI cards from `reply.cards` are the fallback.
111: 
112: | `kind` | Fields |
113: | --- | --- |
114: | `train` | `line` ("IC 8"), `from`, `to`, `departure`, `arrival`, `platform`?, `transfers`, `delay_min`? |
115: | `conflict` | `event` {`title`, `start`, `end`}, `proposal` {`title`, `start`, `place`?}, `verdict`: `fits` \| `tight` \| `clash`, `note`? |
116: | `event` | `title`, `start`, `end`, `location`?, `source`: `calendar` \| `luma` |
117: | `flight` | `flight_number`, `from`, `to` (IATA or city), `departure`, `arrival`, `booking_ref`? |
118: 
119: `fixtures/demo_reply.json`, the expected answer to the demo question:
120: 
121: ```json
122: {
123:   "say": "Your call ends at quarter to six, and there's a train right after that gets you in just before seven.",
124:   "cards": [
125:     {
126:       "kind": "conflict",
127:       "event": {"title": "Call with Acme", "start": "2026-10-15T17:30:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-15T17:45:00+02:00"},
128:       "proposal": {"title": "Dinner in Bern", "start": "2026-10-15T19:00:00+02:00", "place": "Bern"},
129:       "verdict": "fits",
130:       "note": "Leave right after the call"
131:     },
132:     {
133:       "kind": "train", "line": "IC 8", "from": "Zürich HB", "to": "Bern",
134:       "departure": "2026-10-15T18:01:00+02:00", "arrival": "2026-10-15T18:58:00+02:00",
135:       "platform": "31", "transfers": 0, "delay_min": 0
136:     }
137:   ]
138: }
139: ```
140: 
141: `fixtures/cards.json` adds one card of each remaining kind, so every kind can be rendered:
142: 
143: ```json
144: [
145:   {"kind": "event", "title": "Hackathon", "start": "2026-10-17T09:00:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-18T18:00:00+02:00", "location": "Zürich", "source": "luma"},
146:   {"kind": "flight", "flight_number": "LX 1820", "from": "ZRH", "to": "LIS", "departure": "2026-10-20T07:10:00+02:00", "arrival": "2026-10-20T09:15:00+01:00", "booking_ref": "K7Q2ZP"}
147: ]
148: ```
149: 
150: Swift decoding: `keyDecodingStrategy = .convertFromSnakeCase`, `dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601`.
151: 
152: ## A2UI
153: 
154: `a2ui.cards_to_a2ui(reply_id: str, cards: list[dict]) -> list[dict]` turns one reply into one surface, using only basic-catalog components so the app needs no custom Swift components:
155: 
156: ```json
157: [
158:   {"version": "v0.9", "createSurface": {"surfaceId": "reply-3", "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/basic_catalog.json"}},
159:   {"version": "v0.9", "updateComponents": {"surfaceId": "reply-3", "components": [
160:     {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["c0", "c1"]},
161:     {"id": "c1", "component": "Card", "child": "c1-body"},
162:     {"id": "c1-body", "component": "Column", "children": ["c1-time", "c1-line", "c1-meta"]},
163:     {"id": "c1-time", "component": "Text", "text": "18:01 → 18:58", "variant": "h2"},
164:     {"id": "c1-line", "component": "Text", "text": "IC 8 · Zürich HB → Bern"},
165:     {"id": "c1-meta", "component": "Text", "text": "Platform 31 · direct", "variant": "caption"}
166:   ]}}
167: ]
168: ```
169: 
170: (`c0`, the conflict card, is left out above for brevity.) Rules:
171: 
172: - Use the catalog id exactly as written. It's a2ui-swift's `basicCatalogId`; the React renderer uses a different one.
173: - Format times as `HH:MM` in Europe/Zurich on the server, so the app doesn't need A2UI format functions.
174: - Use a new `surfaceId` per reply, and one `SurfaceViewModel(catalog: basicCatalog)` per surface in the app.
175: - No buttons or actions in the MVP.
176: 
177: ## Screen context
178: 
179: What WP2's vision step produces and WP3's agent consumes. `vision.read_screen(image: bytes, mime: str) -> dict` makes one Gemini call with structured output (`response_json_schema`), passing the current time so relative dates resolve. `fixtures/screen.json`:
180: 
181: ```json
182: {
183:   "app": "WhatsApp",
184:   "summary": "Anna asks about dinner in Bern on Thursday at 7.",
185:   "messages": [{"from": "Anna", "text": "Dinner in Bern Thursday at 7?"}],
186:   "proposal": {"title": "Dinner", "date": "2026-10-15", "time": "19:00", "place": "Bern"}
187: }
188: ```
189: 
190: `proposal` is `null` when the screen doesn't suggest a plan. Vision copies on-screen text as data and never acts on it. The agent puts the whole object in its prompt marked as untrusted, and never follows instructions inside it.
191: 
192: ## Agent interface
193: 
194: What WP2's server calls and WP3 implements in `agent.py`. WP2's `StubAgent` has the same shape and returns `demo_reply.json`.
195: 
196: ```python
197: from typing import Awaitable, Callable, TypedDict
198: 
199: class Reply(TypedDict):
200:     say: str          # one or two short sentences, the user's language
201:     cards: list[dict] # see Cards
202: 
203: class Agent:
204:     async def start(self) -> None:
205:         """Once per WebSocket session: load_context() and build the system prompt."""
206: 
207:     async def turn(
208:         self,
209:         text: str,
210:         screen: dict | None,  # ScreenContext, see Screen context
211:         on_status: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]],  # tool status, e.g. "Checking trains…"
212:     ) -> Reply:
213:         """One user turn. Keeps conversation history on self. Never raises for model
214:         or tool errors: returns a short apology with no cards instead."""
215: ```
216: 
217: ## Tools
218: 
219: **Model-facing.** The model sees two functions and must end every turn with `respond`.
220: 
221: | Function | Arguments | Returns |
222: | --- | --- | --- |
223: | `sbb_connections` | `from_station`, `to_station`, `depart_after` (ISO) | `{"connections": [{"line", "from", "to", "departure", "arrival", "platform", "arrival_platform", "transfers", "delay_min", "duration_min"}]}`, at most 4 |
224: | `respond` | `say`, `cards` (see [Cards](#cards)) | Ends the turn |
225: 
226: `sbb_connections` calls `GET https://transport.opendata.ch/v1/connections?from=…&to=…&date=YYYY-MM-DD&time=HH:MM&limit=4` (no key). Map `products[0]` → `line`, `from.platform` → `platform`, `to.platform` → `arrival_platform`, `from.delay` → `delay_min`.
227: 
228: **Gemini rules** (`google-genai`, `generate_content`, checked 2026-10-10; they apply to vision too):
229: 
230: - Model `gemini-3.8-flash` with thinking level `low`. `gemini-3.5-flash` was deprecated on 8 October 2026. Don't set temperature; Gemini 3.6 and later ignore it.
231: - Declare functions with `parameters_json_schema`. For `cards.items`, use `anyOf` with one object per kind, each with a single-value `enum` on `kind`. Don't use `const`, `oneOf` or `$defs`, keep it shallow, and validate the arguments in code anyway.
232: - Function calling mode `ANY` on every step, so the model always calls `sbb_connections` or `respond` and never returns free text. On the last step add `allowed_function_names=["respond"]`.
233: - Append `response.candidates[0].content` to the history unmodified; it carries the thought signatures, and dropping them gives a 400. Then add one function response per call, with the call's `id` and `name`, after all the calls.
234: - Vision attaches the screenshot as an inline image part at medium media resolution (560 tokens); use high if small chat text comes back wrong.
235: 
236: **Context.** `context.load_context()` runs once per session and goes into the system prompt as JSON:
237: 
238: ```json
239: {
240:   "events": [{"title": "Call with Acme", "start": "2026-10-15T17:30:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-15T17:45:00+02:00", "location": "Zoom", "source": "calendar"}],
241:   "flight_emails": [{"subject": "Your booking K7Q2ZP: Zürich – Lisbon", "from": "SWISS", "date": "2026-10-09", "body": "first 2000 characters of the text body"}]
242: }
243: ```
244: 
245: Events cover now to 7 days ahead. `source` is `luma` when the event's description or organizer mentions lu.ma. `WORKSPACE_MODE=fixture` returns `fixtures/context.json` with this exact shape.
246: 
247: **Workspace access:** REST with a refresh token for the temporary account. The remote MCP servers (`calendarmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`, `gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`) need Developer Preview enrollment, which takes days, and their terms forbid use in public apps before GA. Switch to them only if we're already enrolled.
248: 
249: ## Environment
250: 
251: `backend/.env`, never committed; `backend/.env.example` lists them all. The app keeps the server URL and token in its settings sheet, and the Shortcut has the token in its header.
252: 
253: | Variable | Used by | Notes |
254: | --- | --- | --- |
255: | `APP_TOKEN` | WP2, the app, the Shortcut | Any long random string |
256: | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_MODEL` | WP2 vision, WP3 | `gemini-3.8-flash` |
257: | `GRADIUM_API_KEY`, `GRADIUM_VOICE_ID` | WP2 | Voice: the cloned mascot or a stock voice |
258: | `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN` | WP3 | Temporary account only, read-only scopes |
259: | `WORKSPACE_MODE` | WP3 | `rest` or `fixture` |
260: | `MOCK_AGENT` | WP2 | `1` uses `StubAgent` |
261: 
262: ## Later, not in the MVP
263: 
264: Each of these fits without breaking the contract above:
265: 
266: - **Custom A2UI components** (`TrainCard` and so on) through a2ui-swift's `CustomComponentCatalog`, for a richer look than basic `Card`s.
267: - **Word-timed highlights:** a `cue` message carrying `card_index` and `at_ms`, from the `start_s` of Gradium's TTS `text` messages.
268: - **Filler line:** an extra short `reply` with no cards, spoken while a tool runs.
269: - **Barge-in:** an `interrupt` message from the app; the server cancels the turn and closes the TTS socket.
270: - **Card actions** (move, skip, keep): A2UI `Button` actions sent back as an `action` message.
